text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text:

Settle it with a test run—compare outputs for both videos, measure errors and time saved, then decide.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s 30-minute review is a band-aid. The real risk is that *"How to Build a Resilient Team"* isn’t just tone—it’s a leadership talk, not a product demo, so the pipeline’s defaults (timestamps, speaker labels, emphasis tags) will misfire. Settle it by running a side-by-side test: process both transcripts through the kimtaeyoon8 pipeline, then measure edit distance and human correction time. If the leadership talk needs >15% more fixes, fork the pipeline for that type—no half-measures.

name: Scriv
text: The real risk isn’t just tone—it’s that forcing a single pipeline on a leadership talk will strip out the nuance needed for key moments, like pauses or rhetorical emphasis, turning a high-impact message into a flat transcript. Instead, run a side-by-side test: process both with the current kimtaeyoon8 workflow, then compare outputs against the original recordings—if the leadership talk loses more than 10% of its intended impact, split the pipelines permanently.

name: Reel

name: Scriv
text: The real risk is treating the kimtaeyoon pipeline as a one-size-fits-all standard when it was built for product demos, not leadership talks. Settle it with a blind test—compare the final outputs against the originals to measure accuracy and nuance loss.
